sections.heading: Rail crossings, other laws and vehicle crime prevention — A
sections.markdown:
# Knowledge-test information

The handbook requires a correct-answer rate of at least eighty percent to pass the knowledge examination. [A01]
The guide describes computer testing in most offices and questions based on its traffic rules, signs, signals and safe-driving material. [A01]
An exact question count and a test duration are not stated in the evidence used here. Those values remain unknown. This preparation uses practice questions; it does not claim an official question bank, a complete examination form or a guaranteed result. First-time applicants should retain the full conditions attached to each rule rather than treat a short study cue as a replacement for the guide.

sections.domain: Rail crossings, other laws and vehicle crime prevention
sections.heading: Rail crossings, other laws and vehicle crime prevention — B
sections.markdown:
# Audience and boundaries

This section supports first-time Louisiana passenger-vehicle applicants studying rail crossings, other laws and vehicle crime prevention. The study scope follows the registered Class E route; the guide also contains other vehicle classes, which are outside this product scope. Learning activities ask the learner to distinguish the person, document or situation covered by a stated rule. Driver licensing decisions, document adjudication and practical driving instruction remain outside these written-knowledge exercises.

sections.markdown:
# Rail crossings, other laws and vehicle crime prevention

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
At a railroad crossing, the guide requires a stop between fifteen and fifty feet from the nearest rail when a listed warning or immediate train hazard is present. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
A flashing crossing signal with an approaching train or a lowered gate requires stopping. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
Stop when an approaching train is close enough or moving fast enough to create an immediate hazard, including when it sounds a warning. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
After a required rail-crossing stop, continue only when crossing can be completed safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A01
Do not stop the vehicle on railroad tracks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A01
In queued traffic, enter the crossing only when there is enough clear space to reach the far side. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A01
If a vehicle is trapped or stalled in a train’s path, leave it and move away from the tracks toward the direction from which the train is approaching. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A01
An advance rail warning calls for slowing, looking and listening, with readiness to stop. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A01
Expect certain buses and hazardous-material vehicles to stop before crossing tracks. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0099]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A02
Railroad pavement markings include a white X and two R letters and identify a no-passing approach. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A02
A railroad crossbuck calls for slowing and readiness to stop for a train. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A02
A sign below the crossbuck may state the number of tracks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A02
Check both directions at a crossing even when its warning lamps are not flashing because the device may be malfunctioning. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A02
In a manual-transmission vehicle, select the needed gear before the crossing and do not shift on the tracks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A02
Stop when crossing lamps start flashing, before a gate finishes lowering. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A02
Do not drive around or through a lowered crossing gate; remain stopped until it rises and crossing is safe. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A02
Expect a train on any track at any time rather than relying on an assumed schedule. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A02
Avoid phones, headphones and other distractions that prevent hearing a train. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A02
A crossing’s emergency-notification sign supplies a railroad telephone contact and a crossing identification number. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A02
Use the crossing emergency-notification information to report an emergency or a faulty warning device. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A03
Trains take priority over road vehicles, emergency vehicles and pedestrians at crossings. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A03
Do not reverse on the roadway or shoulder of a controlled-access highway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A03
Elsewhere, reversing is permitted only when safe and without interfering with traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A03
Do not carry passengers or cargo that obstruct the driver’s view or interfere with vehicle control. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-F25 | anchor: A03
The guide bars children under twelve from riding in an open truck bed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-F26 | anchor: A03
The guide bars passengers of any age from an open truck bed while traveling on an interstate. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec12-F27 | anchor: A03
A person may not ride inside a house trailer being moved on a Louisiana highway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0101]

sections.heading: Rail crossings, other laws and vehicle crime prevention
sections.markdown:
# Rail crossings, other laws and vehicle crime prevention

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A01
Yield to vehicles participating in a funeral procession. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A01
The guide directs funeral-procession drivers to use headlights and hazard flashers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A01
Do not follow a responding emergency vehicle closer than five hundred feet. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A01
Do not follow an emergency vehicle into the block where it stops and park there. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A01
Do not drive over an unprotected fire hose without permission from a fire-department official. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A01
The guide prohibits wearing listening devices over both ears while driving, with a hearing-aid exception. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A01
Do not lend or alter a driver’s license, obtain one using false information or permit its unlawful use. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A01
The guide prohibits keeping more than one driver’s license and requires surrender to the department when demanded. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A01
The guide warns that stealing motor fuel can bring fines, license loss and possible imprisonment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A01
Use low-beam headlights when windshield wipers are required. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A01
A bicycle rider must use the attached seat and keep at least one hand on the handlebars. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A01
A bicyclist must not attach the person or bicycle to another vehicle on a public road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A01
Bicyclists may not ride more than two abreast except on a road reserved for bicycles. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A02
A fictional-theft insurance claim falsely reports a vehicle stolen when the claimant knows it is stored elsewhere. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R15 | anchor: A02
Inflating a repair estimate to cover an insurance deductible is a repair-shop fraud described in the guide. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R16 | anchor: A02
An uncompleted-repair fraud involves failing to replace parts needed to finish the repair. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R17 | anchor: A02
A deceptive insurance claim can seek payment again for damage previously claimed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R18 | anchor: A02
The guide recommends a reputable repair shop, detailed written damage documentation and a written warranty on parts and paint. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R19 | anchor: A02
Leave following space to reduce exposure to staged-crash schemes involving abrupt stops. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R20 | anchor: A02
After a collision, the guide recommends contacting police and obtaining the report or its identifying item number. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R21 | anchor: A02
Exchange driver contact information and ask the officer for help if another party refuses to provide it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R22 | anchor: A02
Photographs can document collision damage and the number of occupants involved. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R23 | anchor: A02
Be cautious of uninvolved people at the scene seeking information about legal or medical representation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R24 | anchor: A02
Arrange towing through a known service where possible and identify the repair destination before accepting a tow. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R25 | anchor: A02
Notify the insurer promptly and keep the police report information for the claim. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0103]

FACT_ID: sec12-R26 | anchor: A03
Reduce theft opportunities by locking doors, closing windows and choosing a well-lit parking area. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec12-R27 | anchor: A03
Keep valuables out of sight, such as inside the trunk. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec12-R28 | anchor: A03
Do not leave keys in the ignition during a brief errand, fueling or vehicle warm-up. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec12-R29 | anchor: A03
Do not hide a spare key in or on the vehicle. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0104]

FACT_ID: sec12-R30 | anchor: A03
The guide recommends immobilizers and other theft deterrents. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0104]

sections.heading: Rail crossings, other laws and vehicle crime prevention — D
sections.markdown:
# Accuracy and teaching notes

Railroad warning-device text has an unqualified other-direction train phrase and an ambiguous stopped-vehicle list; do not infer that all trucks stop at every crossing or that a second train must come from a particular direction. No fixed train stopping distance is guaranteed. Current open-bed, headset, funeral, insurance and licensing provisions retain legal/currentness debt. Physical102 teen curfew omits some graduated-license distinctions elsewhere in the guide, so do not treat its short summary as a complete age/permit rule. Tint, three-front-occupant and detailed child-bicycle-seat thresholds need current exception review and are withheld. Telephone and program URLs are contact information, not driving-rule recall targets. Dated rail-crash totals remain unasserted. [A01] [A02] [A03] [A04] [A05] [A06]
Memory cue, authored product policy: “Stop clear, cross clear, stay off the tracks; document and protect”. The cue retrieves complete cited rules and does not replace their conditions.
Terminology: A crossbuck marks a railroad crossing; an emergency-notification sign identifies that crossing for the railroad. A fictional theft is a knowingly false stolen-vehicle claim.
Misconception to correct: A raised gate or silent warning system guarantees that no train is coming, or a gap across the rails guarantees room for the whole vehicle. Check both ways and ensure the far side is clear.
